title: Vault daemon-churn: decide on global basic-memory ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=false (operator-owned — affects all 24 bm projects)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the perpetual vault git-churn + a latent corruption risk. basic-memory's daemon has ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=true (~/.basic-memory/config.json, GLOBAL to all 24 projects), so on every sync it re-serializes vault/**/*.md frontmatter: adds 'permalink: a-plus-maxing/<path>' (206/539 files lack it), folds long titles, strips trailing newlines — and DESTRUCTIVELY mangles {placeholder}/flow-collection/inline-comment YAML on template files (e.g. _template.md: 'name: {x}' -> 'name:\n  x: null'). Never committed (the stash-and-discard pattern protected against it), so no data lost, but it's the churn source + a corruption risk if ever committed.

COMPLETE FIX (operator's call — global, affects 23 other bm projects): set ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=false in ~/.basic-memory/config.json (a .bak exists), restart the bm daemon, then 'git restore vault/' in a-plus-maxing -> permanently clean tree. Effect elsewhere: daemon stops auto-injecting permalink-frontmatter into hand-authored files on sync; write_note-created notes are unaffected (frontmatter added at write time); indexing/search/link-resolution still work (title/path fallback). Trivially reversible. No per-project scope exists (one global config + one shared memory.db).

INTERIM (in place now): the don't-commit-vault-daemon-churn discipline + the cross-worktree model are documented in CLAUDE.md (Conventions). Optional hardening: quote template {placeholders} so the daemon's re-serialization is idempotent even if churn is committed.

title: Cap DNA-export decompression size in dna.land (review SEC-205-01)
description: PR #205 /review-pr security finding SEC-205-01 (conf 90, impact 3). dna.land copies a zip member / reads a .txt UNBOUNDED: a 204KB zip → a 209MB landed file (1027x amplification); a 150MB single-line .txt → 477MB RSS. FIX (if approved): stream the zip-member copy with a running byte counter, raise ValueError past a generous ceiling (~100-200MB; real 23andMe ~15-25MB), delete the partial on raise; same size check on the .txt path via source.stat().st_size. Deferred from PR #205 — operator decision required.
notes: S85 wave-A security review (MED-2): the uncapped zip-member decompression now ALSO exists in scripts/ingest/adapters/healthkit.py:124-125 (Apple Health export.xml extraction, mirroring dna.land) — executed: a 510KiB zip extracted a 500MiB member (1029x), and dna.land 514x. Disk exhaustion (memory bounded: copyfileobj streams to disk, iterparse clears). DEFERRED per operator (07f6 still open, revisit later). When addressed, cap BOTH dna.py:96-97 and healthkit.py:124-125 with a running byte-counter + unlink-partial-on-over (the multipart _stage_file pattern).
